newsitem.title: USA: Dole stresses conservatism in South.
newsitem.headline: Dole stresses conservatism in South.

text.p: Republican presidential nominee Bob Dole kicked off a Southern campaign swing on Wednesday by stressing his conservatism in a region that been moving more toward his party in recent years.

"We want to carry the South, all the way, solid all the way, maybe not Arkansas but everywhere else," Dole said. "This is a state we must win, this is a state we should win. I'm a conservative, he's a liberal, don't let him fool you."

He warned voters at a sparsely attended rally at the airport in Macon not to be hoodwinked by President Bill Clinton's recent move to the political middle, exclaiming, "he's a liberal, he's a liberal, he's a liberal."

From Georgia, Dole heads to Florida, where he is in a close race with Clinton in what usually has been a reliably Republican state. Later this week Dole will add Louisiana, Alabama and Texas to his Southern tour.
Campaign strategists are focused on the South, which has been steadily moving to the Republicans in recent years, and the vote-rich state of California.

"We're solidified, I'm nervously optimistic," said Warren Tompkins, Dole's Southern strategist, saying Republicans had not been able to keep up with Democratic spending in the region during the summer but were making headway.

With less than two weeks before the election, Dole appeared to be a candidate still searching for a message that will sell with voters. He has emphasised his plan for a 15 percent tax cut this week, toning down -- but not ending -- the sharp attacks on Clinton's character that had been the staple of recent campaign speeches.

"We want to do it (cut taxes). President Clinton says he can't do it and that's why we want another president, someone who will cut your taxes," Dole said, calling his $548 billion tax plan "a little tax cut."
Democrats have charged that Dole cannot fulfil his promise to reduce taxes and balance the budget at the same time without cutting deeply into popular social programmes.

Dole's stump speech also mixed in a host of conservative staples. He called for constitutional amendments to balance the budget and ban flag burning and promised to sign legislation barring certain late-term abortions.

Some recent polls have suggested that Dole's strategy of attacking the ethics of the Clinton administration are not going over well with voters, but supporters at the airport at Georgia called the issue important.
"I'm convinced people out there, they're going to have a miracle of conscience and pull the right lever (on election day)," said Virginia Hooper from Warner Robins, Georgia.
